## f3be696a1ae4

**Advertised override contract is nonfunctional on source `1ea274054d712cc32964067e6ad3a2ff8cf658acbeaac173a4eff37b7d4b35ab`.** `AXES` advertises controls including `grid_h`, `grid_w`, `palette_kind`, `anchor_corner`, `asymmetry_force`, `palette_size`, `position_bias`, `n_distinct_colors`, and helpful `texture` values, but `generate()` draws those properties directly from one RNG and never consumes those nondegenerate overrides. `self_check()` also does not verify requested overrides.

Exact reproduction uses `seed=17`, `sample_index=4`, `difficulty="hard"`. The default call and all of the following return the identical grid SHA-256 `3d9be36510386fc902e508db235fe191c45063c263f5ef3640e7bb5d8cf27672` and pass `self_check`: `grid_h=14, grid_w=16`; `texture="cool"`; and the combined request `grid_h=14, grid_w=16, palette_kind="warm", anchor_corner=True, asymmetry_force=True, palette_size=1, position_bias="varied", n_distinct_colors=1, texture="warm"`. The observed grid is height 11 rather than 14 and contains two non-axis colors `[1,4]` rather than one. This makes forced-axis curriculum requests silently dishonest even though the returned puzzle itself remains rule-lawful.

Reproducer and complete observations: `checks/audit/f3be696a1ae4/override_probe.py` and `checks/audit/f3be696a1ae4/override_probe.json`. Run from `WORK/repo` with `python3 ../checks/audit/f3be696a1ae4/override_probe.py` under the packet runtime.
